then.text: Come back at dusk when the lanterns are lit. Bring a flask. The Tor is brisk and so, I'm told, am I.

else.text: Well, hello. You've the look of someone who climbed the Tor in the wrong shoes. I'm Morwen. I keep the Fae Stone up here, between the sheep and a surprising number of kites.
Up the Tor in the dark, were you? Brave. Or lost. The two look the same from here.
Fae creatures don't fight fair, love. They fight interesting. Let's see if you can keep up.
The Fae Stone. It won't teach your team anything new on the road, I'm afraid. It just makes the little folk a good deal less cross with you.
That's worth more than a field ability, mind. Ask anyone who's ever stepped on a fairy ring.
{player} received the Fae Stone!
Your phone buzzes. Professor Garside, who is eating something crunchy.
{player}! The Fae Stone! Five! The hum's changed key, and I'm told that's a good thing. Whatever's been grumbling in that orchard has gone from a growl to a purr.
Now, the Enclosure has been busy in the far west. Sir Rupert Ashcombe, Regional Director. He has a hat, a briefcase and a very small moustache.
Dartmoor, then Tintagel, then Cornwall. He's after something in a tin mine, apparently. Mind the knockers. They knock back.
And do stop at the orchard on your way down. Morwen says it's been listening.
Down in the Levels, the Wardens quietly rolled up their 'flood risk' tape and went home.

then.text: The old apple trees stand in a loose circle, heavy with fruit. A warm, green breath moves through the leaves. He's near, and he's happy.

else.text: The Fae Stone grows warm in your pocket. The apple trees lean in. Somewhere under the roots, something very old clears its throat.
A face made of leaves opens its eyes in the bark. Moss for a beard. Pipe-smoke for a breath. He looks at you the way an oak looks at a sapling.

then.text: The Green Man steps out of the bark and falls in beside you, shedding a small leaf with each stride. The orchard sighs, as if a long argument had finally been settled.

else.text: The Green Man melts back into the trunk with a rustle like a wry laugh. The orchard stills. He will wait, if you want to try again.

then.text: The hedge around the orchard is thick with blossom that wasn't there this morning. Where the Wardens' fence stood, hawthorn has taken over.
A low hum rises from the roots. It's friendly, but firm. He isn't ready for you yet. Perhaps the Keeper's Stone will help.

else.text: An orchard tucked into the corner of the Tor. Apple trees older than the road. In the middle stands a gnarled trunk with a roll of orange plastic fencing wrapped around it.
Right, lads, get the fence round it. Orchard's been reclassified. 'Heritage Green Space, Phase Three'.
And put that sign up. 'No Walking. No Wildlife. No Joy.'
Oi! Hang on! That tree is, like, five hundred years old!
Kit comes pounding up the path, out of breath, one hand on a stitch, the other waving a phone.
{player}! I followed you. I'm sorry. I didn't want to miss it, and I definitely didn't want to be on their side. Not this time.
Pull that fence off. I'll take the signs. I'm at least good at being annoying on camera.
You tug at the fencing together. It bites back, tangling round your wrists. A Warden steps up with a mallet and a clipboard.
Sir, madam, this is a Heritage Green Space. You will need a permit. It is a nine-part form.
The tree opens its eyes. A face of bark and leaves, with moss for a beard. Every apple in the orchard turns to look at the Wardens.
The fencing sprouts. First leaves, then thorns, then a thick, cheerful tangle of hawthorn blossom that swallows the stakes whole.
That's. That's not in the plan. Is it in the plan?
The Wardens drop their mallets and leave by the shortest route, which is down. They are very quick downhill.
Okay. OKAY. I have never been this happy to see a tree.
The Green Man looks at you both for a long, unhurried moment. Then he breathes out, and the blossom drifts down like snow.
He is not ready. Not yet. A low voice rolls through the roots, slow as sap: the Keeper's Stone first, small walker. Then we shall talk.
He said Keeper's Stone, right? I'm not imagining it? Morwen's at the top. I'll... go and find a cup of something. Very strong.
